Title: Effectiveness of the Mental Health First Aid programme for general nursing students in Hong Kong: A randomised controlled trial
Author: Hung, Chow, Chien, and Wong
Comment: The paper does not report a binary correct-recognition proportion, event counts, or an odds ratio. Following the synthesis contract, the six-month continuous score was converted: pooled SD from the explicitly reported arm SDs and ITT arm sizes = 0.495; SMD (MHFA minus control) = (2.82−2.29)/0.495 = 1.070; SE(SMD) = sqrt[(182+176)/(182×176) + 1.070²/(2×(182+176−2))] = 0.113. Applying log OR = SMD×π/√3 gives log OR = 1.941 and SE(log OR) = 0.205; OR = 6.968, with derived 95% CI 4.662 to 10.416. The randomised arm sizes were used because the paper states intention-to-treat analysis with last-observation-carried-forward imputation; although 167 experimental and 165 control participants completed the follow-up questionnaire, Table 2 does not provide separate analysed denominators. This conversion assumes the continuous recognition score is an acceptable proxy for the planned binary outcome. The reported F(2,355)=36.56 and partial ηp²=0.17 are for the overall time-by-group interaction, not a simple six-month arm comparison, so they were not entered as the row's test statistic/effect size.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Experimental group: 12-hour Mental Health First Aid programme') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Design Type: Two-arm waitlist randomised controlled trial with repeated assessments and intention-to-treat last-observation-carried-forward analysis
Study Environment: Undergraduate general nursing programme at a tertiary institution
Country: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, China
Content length: 12 hours in four three-hour sessions over one month
Topic of Content: Recognition of depression and other mental health problems and strategies for providing assistance
interaction_type: Small-group interactive teaching and learning activities
Recruitment source: One tertiary institution in Hong Kong
Outcome type: Continuous recognition score used as a proxy for binary correct recognition
Outcome measurement: Mental Health Literacy Scale (Chinese version), depression scenario; each correct answer received one mark and a higher score indicated better mental health knowledge
outcome_family: correct recognition of depression in a case vignette
effect_direction: Higher values indicate better depression recognition; OR > 1 favours MHFA

Title: Mental health first aid training for high school teachers: a cluster randomized trial
Author: Jorm et al.
Comment: The reported OR is the authors’ mixed-effects pre-to-6-month-follow-up group-by-occasion interaction estimate, accounting for repeated observations and clustering within schools; it is not a simple follow-up-only arm odds ratio. The log OR (1.1282) was derived as ln(3.09), and SE(log OR) (0.7094) was derived from the reported 95% CI as [ln(12.43) − ln(0.77)]/(2×1.96). Arm-specific follow-up denominators and event counts were not reported, so they were left null; baseline sample sizes (221 intervention and 106 control) were not substituted for final analyzed Ns. Follow-up percentages are reported descriptively only and were not used to reconstruct counts.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Modified Youth Mental Health First Aid training') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Design Type: Cluster-randomized controlled trial with mixed-effects longitudinal analysis
domain: Mental health literacy / Mental Health First Aid
Medium: Face-to-face modified Youth Mental Health First Aid course delivered at participants’ schools
Content length: Two one-day parts of seven hours each; the majority received the abbreviated 7-hour training
Topic of Content: Recognition and initial assistance for adolescent mental health problems, including depression
Participant type: High school teachers and other education staff working with Years 8–10
Recruitment source: Government, Catholic, and independent South Australian high schools invited through the South Australian Department of Education and Children’s Services
Outcome measurement: Percentage mentioning “depression” in an open-ended response to a major-depressive-episode vignette
outcome_family: correct recognition of depression in a case vignette
effect_direction: OR > 1 indicates better depression recognition with MHFA

Title: Mental health first aid training by e-learning: a randomized controlled trial
Author: Anthony F. Jorm, Betty A. Kitchener, Julie-Anne Fischer, Stefan Cvetkovski
Comment: The paper reported only follow-up percentages and explicitly did not test depression recognition inferentially because of a ceiling effect. Follow-up analyzed denominators by arm were not stated. Following the synthesis contract, randomized denominators were used: waiting list n=84, manual n=88, CD n=90. Events were reconstructed by multiplying each reported percentage by its randomized denominator and rounding to the nearest whole participant: waiting list 93.6%×84→79; manual 94.8%×88→83; CD 97.0%×90→87. The two eligible MHFA arms were combined to 170/178. Derived OR=(170/8)/(79/5)=1.3449; log(OR)=0.2962; SE[log(OR)]=sqrt(1/170+1/8+1/79+1/5)=0.5861. These reconstructed counts do not exactly reproduce the published percentages and should be treated as an assumption-based estimate using randomized rather than observed follow-up denominators.
Design Type: Individually randomized three-group parallel controlled trial
domain: Mental health literacy / Mental Health First Aid
Study Environment: Online questionnaires; community participants across Australia completed MHFA materials independently
Medium: MHFA e-learning CD or printed MHFA manual
Topic of Content: Recognition of mental disorders and provision of mental health first aid
Recruitment source: Online advertisements, flyers in university libraries and community and mental health centres, and local newspaper/newsletter advertisements across Australia
Outcome measurement: Open-ended response to 'From the information given, what, if anything, is wrong with Mary?'; 'depression' was correct
outcome_family: correct recognition of depression in a case vignette
effect_direction: OR > 1 indicates better depression recognition with MHFA

Title: Effectiveness of Mental Health First Aid training in Denmark: a randomized trial in waitlist design
Author: Jensen et al.
Comment: Raw correct-recognition counts were not reported, so events were not reconstructed from rounded percentages. For synthesis, using the authors' reported OR and 95% CI gives log(OR) = 0.5068 and SE[log(OR)] = [ln(2.95) - ln(0.93)]/(2×1.96) = 0.2946. These two derived values are recorded here because the result schema has no dedicated log-OR or SE(log-OR) fields. The paper reports intention-to-treat multiple imputation, but it does not explicitly describe whether this OR was adjusted for baseline; the trial was not cluster randomized.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Immediate MHFA training intervention group') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Design Type: Individually randomized waitlist-controlled trial with 6-month follow-up and intention-to-treat multiple imputation
domain: Mental health literacy / Mental Health First Aid training
Study Environment: Ten Danish public, private, and nongovernmental workplaces/organizations
Topic of Content: Recognition of mental illness and provision of initial mental health first aid
